explanation.text: Evolution is a population-level process: inherited allele frequencies change across generations. An individual changing during its lifetime is not the same process as a lineage evolving into a new species.

reasoningChain: Describe change across generations in a population.
Link accumulated genetic change to the formation of species.

stem.text: Approximately 95% of bird species living today belong to an evolutionary group known as Neoaves.
Bird species in the Neoaves group are believed to have evolved from a common ancestor that existed around 67 million years ago. The Neoaves that exist today can be divided into four groups:

items: all other Neoaves, referred to as group 4.

stem.text: In 2014, scientists used DNA sequence data from 48 bird species to produce an evolutionary (phylogenetic) tree for the Neoaves. This is shown in Figure 4.1. The evolutionary tree shows possible evolutionary relationships between the four groups of species within the Neoaves.

stem.caption: Figure 4.1
stem.alt: 2014 phylogenetic tree for four Neoaves groups.

stem.text: In 2024, scientists used DNA sequence data from 363 bird species to produce a new evolutionary tree for the four groups of species within the Neoaves. This is shown in Figure 4.2.

stem.caption: Figure 4.2
stem.alt: 2024 phylogenetic tree for four Neoaves groups.

explanation.text: Compare corresponding positions in homologous DNA sequences. Substitutions shared by a subset of species can support a common branch, while greater sequence similarity generally supports a more recent common ancestor.

reasoningChain: Use shared differences and similarities to group the species.

stem.text: During the evolution of some Neoaves species, crossing over during meiosis did not occur in a large section of one chromosome for several million years.
State and explain the effect on genetic diversity of an absence of crossing over.

explanation.text: Alleles at loci on a chromosome can be inherited together as a linked combination. Without crossing over in that region, meiosis cannot create new combinations by exchanging the region between homologues.

reasoningChain: Follow the linked alleles through meiosis without exchange.
Distinguish unchanged combinations from the production of new alleles by mutation.
